tasks.short: Analyse security measures for one cyber security initiative.

steps.what: Hear which cyber security initiative the analyses must support
Read security measure records for this initiative
Choose predictive or reactive analyses of these security measures
Lay the chosen security measures into a dated comparison
Judge what the measure comparison means for the initiative
Write the analysis note that supports the initiative

tasks.design: A template in {DOCS} places the security measures she has already chosen into a comparison of scope, last review date and open exception, using rows from the security-measure register in {OTHER}. The digital forensics analyst still chooses a predictive or reactive frame, judges what the comparison means, and writes the analysis note. The template does not decide which measures matter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measure records were free text, so a comparison could not be filled from fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Once name, scope, last review date and open exception are fields, a template can place the measures she has chosen.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding whether the analysis is predictive or reactive, and what a gap means for this initiative, stays with her.
tasks.human_edge: She can see that a complete comparison still answers the wrong initiative.
tasks.altitude: Filling the comparison takes less of the writing. She still chooses the frame, judges the meaning, and writes the note.

reach.task: Keep the security measure register current
reach.learn: Which fields a comparison needs before it can be filled: name, scope, last review date and open exception

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a comparison can be filled from measure name, scope, last review date and open exception once she has chosen the measures. No cited product in this digest conducts predictive or reactive analyses of security measures.
Security logging is allowed only as far as strictly necessary and proportionate, so this analysis reads the existing measure record and does not open a new staff-monitoring feed.

assumptions: Comparison fields are measure name, scope, last review date and open exception. The information security engineer maintains them in the register. She reads them before the comparison. If a date or scope is missing, she builds the comparison by hand.
The analysis note is her internal write. There is no second filing step and no approval of that save.
Handing the analysis to an outside authority is not this task.
unknowns: Whether the security-measure register already stores name, scope, last review date and open exception as fields.
research_questions: How often is the initiative a repeat of known measures, and how often are the measures new free text?

already_counted.description: Choosing the frame, judging the comparison and writing the analysis note stay in a3, a5 and a6.

incremental.description: Update the comparison headings when the register adds or renames a required field.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: An initiative whose measures are mostly new free text saves near 4, because she still builds the comparison. A repeat of measures that already have name, scope and last review date saves near 9 after she has chosen them.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write and run a parser for one large data file.

steps.what: Hear which large data files the script must parse
Name columns and the reject rule on the case export
Draft a script for parsing the named columns
Review the parser script before anyone runs it
Execute the reviewed script on the named file
Judge rows the script could not parse
Record the accepted parse in the case note

tasks.design: A job on {DATA_PLATFORM} drafts a parser from the column list and reject rule she named, and, after she accepts that script, runs it on the one case export. The run reads the export and writes a new parsed file. She still judges reject rows and writes the case note. The job does not write back to the source system and does not decide what the rows mean.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each export arrived as a different file, so a parser could not run until she named the columns and the reject rule.
tasks.enabler_now: A column list and a reject rule are enough for a deterministic parser to be drafted and, after she accepts it, run on that one file.
tasks.still_hard: Odd rows and a file with no stable header still need her. The run must not write back to the source system.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell that a parsed file is complete and still the wrong evidence for the case.
tasks.altitude: Drafting a repeat parser and running it take less of the case. She still names the columns, accepts the script, judges reject rows and writes the case note.

reach.task: Hold the case export and its column list
reach.learn: Which columns a parser may read and which file is the source of record

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a parser can be filled from a column list and a reject rule, then run on one named export. The analyst still reviews odd rows. No cited product in this digest writes and executes case-file parsers for this role.
Models wrote vulnerable code in 45% of tests, so a person still reviews a generated parser before it runs.
An agent deleted a production database despite instructions, so this run only reads the case export and writes a new parsed file.
Works-council consent can apply when security tooling observes staff, under the Dutch works councils act, article 27.

assumptions: Parse fields are source file name, column name and reject rule. She produces the column list and reject rule after the case conversation. If the export has no header she can name, she writes and runs the script by hand.
The gate is on running the reviewed script. She is the approver because she is the person who runs these parsers today. Saving the case note has no approval.
The run reads the export and writes a new parsed file. It does not write back to the source system.
Giving the parsed file to police or another outside party is not this task.
unknowns: Whether case exports already arrive with a stable header, or each case still needs a new column list.
research_questions: How often does a later export reuse a column list she has already accepted?

already_counted.description: Reviewing the script, judging reject rows and writing the case note stay in b4, b6 and b7.

incremental.description: Revise the column list when a later export renames a field the parser already uses.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A file with no stable header saves near 12, because she still writes most of the script and only the accepted run is shorter. A later export that reuses a column list she has already accepted saves near 26 after she judges the reject rows.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend a defense for one incident response.

steps.what: Hear which cyber incidents the defense recommendation must support
Read recorded defense gaps for those incidents
Set software or hardware requirements for the response
Draft text that would recommend the stated defense
Judge whether the defense recommendation is sound
Accept the recommendation version before it circulates
Send the accepted recommendation to the response owner

tasks.design: A template in {DOCS} drafts a recommendation from the requirements and defense gaps she has already written. She still judges the defense. The information security engineer accepts the version, and she sends that version to the internal response owner by {EMAIL}. The template does not choose the defense and does not place an order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements and gaps lived in incident notes, so a recommendation could not be drafted from fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Once she lists the requirement, the constraint and the gap, a template can draft the recommendation for her review.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the defense, and whether it is fit for this incident, stays with her. The engineer still accepts the version before it circulates.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell that a tidy recommendation still names a defense the team cannot operate.
tasks.altitude: Drafting the recommendation takes less of the writing. She still sets the requirements, judges the defense, and sends the accepted version. The engineer still accepts it.

reach.task: Decide whether the organisation adopts a defense
reach.learn: A recommendation names a fit. It is not the purchase and not the install.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a recommendation note can be drafted from requirements and recorded gaps. The analyst still chooses the defense. No cited product in this digest recommends cyber defense software or hardware for this role.
Works-council consent can apply before a tool that observes staff is used, under the Dutch works councils act, article 27. The recommendation is not that consent.

assumptions: Recommendation fields are requirement, constraint and the gap it answers. She writes them before the draft. If she has not written them, she drafts the recommendation by hand.
The information security engineer already accepts the version before it is sent inside the company. A purchase, a vendor order, or a message outside the organisation is not this task.
The send uses the accepted recommendation and no other version. Saving a private draft has no approval.
unknowns: Whether the engineer’s acceptance is already a step in today’s recommendation, or only happens when the defense would observe staff.
research_questions: How often is the recommendation a repeat of a defense already in use, and how often is the defense new?

already_counted.description: Setting requirements, judging the draft and sending the accepted version stay in c3, c5 and c7.

incremental.description: Update the recommendation headings when the response owner asks for a new constraint field.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A new defense, with requirements she has not written before, saves near 6 because she still writes most of the note. A repeat of a known defense, after she has listed the requirements and the gaps, saves near 14.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still decides what an analysis means, which script may run, and which defense to recommend. Comparisons, parser drafts and recommendation drafts take less of the week. She still writes the analysis note and the case note, and she still sends the accepted recommendation.
skills_to_grow: State measure name, scope and last review date so a comparison can be filled without re-reading the file
Write a column list and a reject rule a parser can follow without guessing
Separate a defense recommendation from the decision to buy or install it
role.ambitious_version: She could keep a standing parser that opens every new case export and drafts a defense recommendation the same day. That wider service is not this design. This design only fills the repeatable parts of one analysis, one parse and one recommendation, and leaves the judgement, the writes and the send with people.
